transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. They've been happening more often, and it's really starting to scare me.
Did these thoughts start after a specific stressful or traumatic event, or have they come on without a clear trigger?

I was already really stressed from working long shifts at my understaffed clinic and studying, but everything fell apart about three weeks ago when I found out I failed a key certification exam. That failure made me feel like I was completely failing everyone, and that is when these dark thoughts really took hold.
Have these symptoms been present for less than 6 months and clearly started after the exam failure, or were you having similar low mood or suicidal thoughts before that?

It has only been about three weeks, starting right after I found out I failed that certification exam. I didn't have this kind of low mood or thoughts of death before that, but since then, it has felt incredibly heavy and constant without letting up.

Since this started, have you also had other depression symptoms like loss of interest or pleasure, changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, poor concentration, or feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

Yes, I've been struggling with almost all of those. I've lost all interest in things I used to love like painting and salsa, my appetite has completely vanished to the point where food tastes like cardboard, and I just feel so useless and hollow inside. My brain also feels constantly foggy, which makes it incredibly hard to study or even make simple decisions.
Did these symptoms begin only after the exam failure and other stressors, or have you had similar depressive episodes before without a clear trigger?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before; this is the very first time I've ever had a depressive episode. Before the exam failure and the intense stress at the clinic, I was always very active with my yoga, painting, and salsa dancing. These feelings only started about three weeks ago after I got those results.
Did your symptoms start only after the exam failure and other stress, or did you have a period of low mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks before that without a clear trigger?

No, I didn't have any period of low mood or loss of interest before the exam. I was definitely feeling stressed and pressured by work and studying, but I was still coping and doing my yoga and painting. The constant heavy feeling and losing interest in everything only took hold about three weeks ago, right after I found out I failed.
Have you had any major stressors or traumatic events around the time these symptoms started, and did the low mood and loss of interest begin within a few days of that event?

Yes, finding out I failed that certification exam was the major trigger, on top of the stress of helping displaced patients at my understaffed clinic after the hurricane season. The deep low mood and losing interest in everything started almost immediately, within just a couple of days of getting that bad news.

Since these symptoms started, have you been able to keep up with work and daily responsibilities, or have the stress and mood symptoms made it hard to function? Also, do the symptoms feel clearly tied to the exam failure and other stressors?

It’s been incredibly hard to function—I’m making more charting errors at work, had to postpone my next exam attempt because I can't focus to study, and I'm dodging calls from my family because I have no energy. These feelings are definitely tied to failing that exam, combined with the constant pressure of our understaffed clinic.
Have you ever had a similar period of depression or loss of interest before this, even if it was milder or not tied to a specific stressor?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt a depression or loss of interest like this, and it feels entirely new and completely overwhelming to me.
Did your symptoms start within a month of the exam failure and other stressors, or did they begin later and seem unrelated to those events?

Yes, they started almost immediately, just a couple of days after I found out I failed the exam three weeks ago. It definitely didn't start later—it hit me right then and has been weighing on me constantly ever since.
Have you had any thoughts of actually harming yourself or making a plan to end your life, or are the thoughts more about not wanting to be here without a plan?

It started with just wishing I wouldn't wake up, but lately I've spent time online reading about painless methods of dying and picturing myself doing it. I don't have a concrete plan set in motion, but it really scares me because it feels much more serious than just a passing thought.

Have you been having any symptoms like intrusive memories, nightmares, feeling on edge, or avoiding reminders of the exam failure or the hurricane-related stress? Or is it mainly a persistent depressed mood and loss of interest without those trauma-related symptoms?

No, I don't have nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge or jumpy. It is really just this persistent, heavy depressed mood and a complete loss of interest in things I used to love like painting and salsa. Instead of feeling highly anxious or on alert, I just feel completely hollow, exhausted, physically slowed down, and empty inside.
Have these symptoms been improving at all since the stressor, or have they stayed severe and constant every day for more than two weeks? Also, have you ever had any similar episodes before?

No, they haven't improved at all and have stayed constant and heavy every single day for the last three weeks since I failed that exam. This is also the very first time I have ever experienced anything like this, as I've never had a similar episode before.

Have you ever had any periods of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks when there was no major stressor or trigger, or has this episode only happened after the exam failure and other stressors?

No, I've never had anything like this happen before; this is the very first time I've ever felt this way. It only started about three weeks ago, right after I failed my certification exam and was dealing with the intense stress and understaffing at the clinic.
Have your symptoms been improving at all as the stress from the exam and work has changed, or do they stay just as severe even when you are away from those stressors?

No, they haven't improved at all and stay just as severe. They have been weighing on me constantly without letting up for the past three weeks, even when I am away from work or trying to relax at home. It feels like there is no escape from this heavy feeling, no matter where I am or what I'm doing.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, or were more talkative, impulsive, or overly confident than usual?
No, I have never experienced a period of feeling unusually energized, irritable, or overly confident like that. My feelings have mostly been the exact opposite—heavy, slow, and completely exhausted.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual since this started? Also, have you noticed any significant weight loss or gain?

I haven't noticed major changes in my sleep, other than just scrolling on the couch until I eventually fall asleep. However, my appetite has completely vanished; on my 12-hour shifts I'll realize I've only forced down half a granola bar, and even my mom's homemade food just sits in the fridge because everything tastes like cardboard. I haven't weighed myself, but I've definitely lost some weight since I am barely eating anything.
Has the low mood and loss of interest continued for at least two weeks even after the stressor was over, or does it only happen while you are dealing with the stressful situation?

The stress from the understaffed clinic and my studies is still ongoing, but these heavy feelings have been constant and continuous for about three weeks now. Since the moment I found out I failed that exam, the low mood and loss of interest haven't let up for even a single day.

Before this episode started, did you have any prior history of depression or similar symptoms, even if they were milder or not tied to a stressful event? Or is this the first time you have ever had symptoms like this?
This is the very first time I have ever experienced symptoms like this. I have never had any history of depression or even mild feelings of low mood before this all happened.
Do your symptoms feel much more intense than you would expect from the stressor, or have they been causing major problems for work, relationships, or daily life for most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, these feelings are incredibly intense and have been causing major problems in my life almost every day for the past three weeks. I've been making more charting errors at the clinic and had to postpone my next certification attempt because I can't keep up with studying. I'm also dodging calls and invites from my friends and family because I just don't have the energy to show up for anyone anymore.
Have your symptoms been improving at all as the stressor changes, or do they remain severe even when you are away from the exam and work stress?

No, they haven't improved at all and remain just as severe. Even when I am at home and completely away from the clinic or my studies, this heavy weight is constantly there without letting up. It has been a persistent, exhausting feeling every single day for the past three weeks.
Since the exam failure and clinic stress started, have you had any nightmares, flashbacks, feeling constantly on edge, or strong avoidance of reminders of those events?

No, I haven't really experienced nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on edge in that way. My struggle has been much more about the heavy sadness, my complete lack of energy, and those dark thoughts about not wanting to be here anymore.

Have your symptoms been steadily present most days for at least two weeks even when you are away from the stressor, or do they mainly come and go only when you are dealing with the stressful situation?

Yes, they have been steadily present every single day for about three weeks now, without letting up at all. It is a continuous, heavy weight that stays with me even when I am at home or away from the clinic and studying, rather than something that just comes and goes. It is just always there, no matter what.
Did these symptoms begin within a month of the stressful event and seem clearly tied to it, or have they continued for months or appeared without a clear trigger?

Yes, they started about three weeks ago, directly after I found out I failed my key certification exam. It felt completely tied to that failure, especially coming on top of the intense stress at the clinic, and the feelings have been constant and unyielding ever since.
Have you ever had a period of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks before this, even when nothing major was going on in your life?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time I have ever felt this way, and I haven't had any periods of depression or loss of interest in the past.

Do you feel the depression started only as a reaction to the exam failure and clinic stress, or do you think it came on independently of those events? Also, has it been steadily improving, staying the same, or getting worse over the past three weeks?

It definitely felt triggered by those events, and failing that certification exam felt like a breaking point after all the intense stress at the clinic. It hasn't been improving at all; it has been weighing on me constantly for the past three weeks and actually feels like it's getting worse as I become more and more overwhelmed.

Did your symptoms start only as a reaction to the exam failure and work stress, or did they begin even without a clear trigger? Also, have they been steadily improving, staying the same, or getting worse over the past few weeks?

They definitely started as a reaction; I was already under so much pressure from the understaffed clinic and studying, but everything spiraled after I failed that exam three weeks ago. Since then, the symptoms haven't let up at all and have been weighing on me constantly. It actually feels like it's getting increasingly overwhelming as time goes on.

Have you had any symptoms like hearing or seeing things other people don't, or feeling hopelessly guilty, worthless, or like you are being punished in a way that feels out of proportion to the situation?

No, I haven't seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't feel like I'm being punished. However, I do feel extremely useless and hollow inside, and since failing that exam, I feel like a complete failure to my patients and my own goals.

Have you had any thoughts that are out of touch with reality, like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or believing you are being punished or are a complete failure in a way that feels fixed and impossible to question?

No, I haven't seen or heard anything that isn't there, and I don't feel out of touch with reality. While I feel like a complete failure because of my exam and feel incredibly down, I know those feelings are just tied to what actually happened.
Did your symptoms begin only after the exam failure and clinic stress, or were you feeling depressed or losing interest before that without any clear trigger?

The stress at the clinic had been building for a while, but I was still managing it with things like yoga and painting. The actual depression and loss of interest only started and became constant about three weeks ago, right after I found out I failed the certification exam. I definitely wasn't feeling this way before that specific trigger.
